title: ManageBuyOffer whose offer ID is 2^53 + 1
description: A ManageBuyOffer operation with offerID 9007199254740993, the first int64 that an IEEE-754 double cannot hold. Decoding is not the problem; building the operation is. An SDK that accepts the ID as a floating-point number encodes 9007199254740992, a different offer, without an error.

shapes.note: int64. Core treats 0 as 'create' and looks any other ID up; a negative ID is rejected. To be confirmed against core source for the guide.

provenance.method: Encoded from XDR-JSON with the stellar-xdr CLI.
provenance.rationale: Hand-built because it is a bare Operation. The operation is well-formed, so we expect core to include it in a ledger (the envelope side) even though no offer with this ID exists and the operation would fail; this has not been run against core. Offer IDs on the public networks are far below 2^53 today.

decoded.why: XDR-JSON carries int64 as a string, so the value is exact.

operations.why: Control: rebuilding the operation with the ID as a decimal string must give the payload's bytes.
Rebuilding with the ID as the language's floating-point number must give the same bytes or fail. Encoding …0020000000000000 (2^53) is the wrong answer.
An empty string is not an ID; reading it as 0 turns an update into 'create a new offer'.
A negative offer ID is rejected by the network.
Only canonical decimal digits are an ID.

notes: Both verdicts were measured on 2026-11-17 with the published npm packages (repro/README.md).
